Author: @Robopoop101
Content:
Apparently, the game had been active for a month before a patch was released in August 30th that might have introduced or activated the stealers. Seems like this is how it is done these days. Release a legitimate and clean game on Steam, wait until it gets its first downloads, before releasing a 'zero day' malware patch. The game will eventually be shut down but the damage will have already been done.

Don't know how Steam is going to be prevent this from happening again in the future, but what we as consumers can do is simple: Do not buy a game as soon as it releases. Wait a couple of months or for a sale and keep a look out for any news. Investing in a good anti virus software that monitors for suspicious system changes or network traffic helps too.

Author: @richardburnaii5165
Content:
Miami seems to have become the big hub of crypto scams.  I lost 10k in 2024, when options trading of crypto was first coming to fruition there was a site that a person introduced me to, I checked it out and everything seemed to be legit, so I set up an account and started reading the tutorials and was watching the charts and such.  I first was just using the "fake funds" to see how well I could do and was getting to know the person I had started chatting with on a personals site.  I was doing really well at predicting the up/down of bitcoin.  So I transferred money over and started using real money, at my peak I had taken the $10k all the way up to $800K that's when I decided to withdraw the funds, that is also when I found out it was just a big elaborate scam.  I felt like such a fool.  

So I went and started tracking everything, one of the best things about block chain is everything can be traced.  I got all the information including wallet addresses, domain registration  details, screenshots, etc. and sent it over to the FBI and state/local police to be told they would look into it.  I have kept checking to see if the site was up and how active the wallets where, then 2 months ago everything seemed to just freeze on the wallets and the website was no longer up.  I still haven't heard from the police.

There are so many of these fake games that just steal from people is a huge problem, I even see them in all the digital stores.

Crypto people have gotten progressively dumber, or forgotten the rules outlined by crypto. Most likely both.

That was over a decade ago. And even today people like Zilla are using information like that to track wallets and see where the money goes. Thats why most people who actually know what they are doing, and get into this kind of activity have multiple separate wallets, and even some in alt accounts, so it cant be traced back to them.
